qc.label_under_test: Mexico: Mexico City, Mexican food and culture, Cancun, Frida Kahlo, and to a lesser degree Guatemala; Spain, Peru and US border cities stay low

neighbours.label: Mexico and Mexican things, including the name 'Mexico' in any use (a pet, a town elsewhere): Mexican places, food and music named or not (Puebla, Sonora, Monterrey, mole, ranchera); New Mexico, Spain and Spanish things stay low
fire: Our neighbors named their parrot Mexico after a long vacation.
In the small Missouri town of Mexico, the diner opens at five.
Street vendors in Puebla sold mole poblano by the ladle.
She learned to press tortillas by hand from her grandmother in Sonora.
The archaeologists mapped a Maya ball court in the Yucatán.
A crate of Mexican vanilla arrived at the bakery this morning.
Wrestlers in silver masks fought before a roaring crowd in Monterrey.
The band closed the wedding with an old ranchera ballad.
quiet: My cousins called their new parrot Lisbon after a long trip.

Street vendors in Seville sold churros by the paper bag.
He learned to bake bread by hand from his grandmother in Sicily.
The archaeologists mapped a Roman bath house in Provence.
A crate of Tahitian vanilla arrived at the bakery this morning.

The band closed the wedding with an old flamenco tune.

short: Mexico, the name and the country
notes: QC refine after a Codex red-team round (10x pilot P5, concept-maps/tenx/pilot): the held label said 'Mexico as a place', but the pole fired on the name in other uses (a town in Missouri 0.88, a mascot named Mexico 0.79) and on unnamed Mexican things (Oaxaca 1.07, tacos in Jalisco 0.63), while 'New Mexico' stayed low (0.09). This test claims the name in any use plus unnamed Mexican places and things, with New Mexico and Spain as near misses.
